attestations.body: Self-review completed (GitHub does not permit approving my own PR). I reviewed correctness, security, maintainability, tests, reliability, design, architecture, and documentation. The pass found and fixed two material gaps before merge: runtime overrides can no longer redirect a clean run to unreviewed model/data paths, and Hub publication now requires a fresh credential-free `token=False` reload plus a held-out fact query. Uploads also replace stale files and verify the exact public file set. Final local checks: locked dependencies, Ruff with a cold cache, 19 pytest tests, exact-token candidate/history scans, CUDA/BF16 full-model preflight, 186 LoRA targets, and 5,411,328 trainable rank-8 parameters. GitHub CI is green. No baseline generation or training has run.

attestations.body:
Focused results review completed across correctness, credential safety, maintainability, tests, reliability, design/architecture, evidence integrity, and documentation accuracy.

The review initially found: (1) the exhausted ladder remained callable from the CLI, (2) several cross-profile observations were worded causally despite concurrent recipe changes, (3) one nine-attempt sentence was ambiguous, and (4) the architecture still showed the historical run path as current. All findings are resolved: `run` now exits 2 before configuration/model loading, comparisons explicitly state their confounds, the count is unambiguous, and the diagram/prose separate current, historical, and future behavior.

Independent recomputation matched all three acceptance decisions, checkpoint selections, metrics, affected IDs, horizons, and evidence hashes. The three Markdown evaluations reproduce byte-for-byte from JSON. Static public-evidence scans found no credential-shaped values, forbidden credential keys, local paths, tracebacks, signed URLs, or active markup. Final checks: Ruff passed, 51 tests passed, 96 installed packages are compatible, GitHub CI passed, and diff hygiene is clean.

No actionable findings remain. This is a review comment rather than self-approval, which GitHub does not permit.
